results.statement: For N=rL and a character descended to L, the character-weighted trace of f slash diag(1,r) from Gamma_0(L) intersect Gamma^0(r) to Gamma_0(L) is cuspidal of level L. Its exact cosets number r if r divides L and r+1 otherwise.
results.hypotheses: Integer k>=2, r prime, N=rL, f in S_k(N,chi_N), chi_N inflated from chi_L; the slash is determinant^(k/2). This includes r=2 and L=1.
results.scope: Finite cosets, inverse character weights, representative independence, transformation law and cusp descent.

results.statement: If r^2 divides N and chi_N descends modulo N/r, E_r=U_r maps S_k(N,chi_N) to S_k(N/r,chi_{N/r}); its trace normalization is E_r f=r^(k/2-1) T(f slash diag(1,r)).
results.hypotheses: Integer k>=2, r prime, r^2 divides N, chi_N descended to N/r.

results.statement: For q occurring exactly once in N and a character descended to N/q, E_q+q^(k/2-1)W_q^N maps S_k(N,chi_N) to S_k(N/q,chi_{N/q}). The chosen partial matrices normalize Gamma_0(N), preserve the descended character and give a choice-independent operator with square chi_{N/q}(q)I.
results.hypotheses: Integer k>=2, q prime, q divides N and q^2 does not divide N, chi_N inflated from chi_{N/q}; matrix [[qx,y],[Nz,q]] with qx-(N/q)yz=1.
results.scope: All four conjugation entries, matrix square, choice independence, rational cusp condition and prime-to-q dilation covariance.

results.statement: The Fourier filter I-V_r E_r applied to level M is cuspidal at level Mr^2 with inflated character, at level Mr when r divides M, and at level M when r^2 divides M and the character descends modulo M/r. Inflation from N to NR with q not dividing R preserves precisely the obstruction to character descent from N to N/q.
results.hypotheses: Integer k>=2, r and q prime; for the conductor assertion q divides N and M=NR with q not dividing R. N and R may share other prime factors.
results.scope: Coefficient telescope, controlled individual-prime level raising, surjective unit reduction and the conductor-kernel CRT lift.

results.statement: If a fixed-character cusp form has each nonzero index divisible by a prime in a finite nonempty admissible set Q, a chosen q in Q can be removed by subtracting V_q phi with phi at level N/q. The residual keeps level N and its character, and is supported on multiples of Q minus q.
results.hypotheses: Integer k>=2; f in S_k(N,chi_N); every q in Q divides N and permits character descent modulo N/q. Support means the union of the multiples of primes in Q.
results.scope: For q occurring once, M=N times the product of squares of the other primes admits one legal matrix at both N and M. Each intermediate level divides M/r_i and its character descends through M/(r_i q). The common-level trace has the exact remaining coefficient factor 1+q^(-1).

results.statement: For f in S_k(N,chi_N), vanishing of a_n whenever gcd(n,D)=1 gives f=sum_{q|gcd(N,D)} V_q h_q with h_q in S_k(N/q,chi_{N/q}), and only primes admitting character descent may contribute. If there are no such primes, f=0.
results.hypotheses: Integer k>=2, N,D>=1, fixed lower-right character; incompatible parity makes the space zero.
results.scope: Arbitrary finite auxiliary prime set, elimination of outside-level and conductor-obstructed primes by Theorem A.1, then admissible-prime extraction at the original level. No arbitrary diamond projection is assumed.

results.statement: A fixed-character cusp form supported only at indices divisible by p is zero when p is outside the level or prevents character descent, and otherwise is V_p of a cusp form at level N/p.
results.hypotheses: Integer k>=2, p prime, fixed character at N.
results.scope: Conductor-kernel shear, group generation and cusp descent; outside-level vanishing uses the good-prime recurrence and complex coefficient bound.

results.statement: For a normalized trivial-character newform, a_p=-w_p p^(k/2-1) when p occurs once in N, and a_p=0 when p^2 divides N.
results.hypotheses: Integer k>=2, trivial character, normalized newform and p prime dividing N; newspace stability and positivity are used.
results.locator: Section 5, proof of the displayed trivial-character formulas, using Theorem 2.3 and Proposition 5.2
results.scope: The finite lowering formulas are proved in Lemma 3.3 and Proposition 3.4. This newspace consequence retains the Petersson and spectral prerequisites; it does not prove ramified-character classification.

earlier_proofs.result: Lemmas 1.0–1.1: Chinese remainder construction and determinant-one integral lifting
Proposition 1.1 and determinant multiplicativity: slash cocycle; cusp and Fourier coordinates
Section 2 after (2.3), Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.3: rational-slash cusp preservation, fixed-character prime stability and coefficient formulas
Theorem 6.1 and its fixed-character extension: complex coefficient bound and finite-dimensional coefficient injection

retained_prerequisites: The elementary integer, finite-field, finite-dimensional algebra and complex/cusp foundations disclosed in lessons 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 9 remain the framework for the fixed-character support proof.
The unrestricted Gamma_1(N) auxiliary-D support statement remains an exact separate proof obligation; arbitrary diamond projection has not been proved to preserve its support hypothesis.

Newspace deductions and multiplicity retain Petersson convergence, integral change of variables, adjoints, positivity and simultaneous finite-dimensional spectral decomposition with their exact programme foundations.
Cross-character prime-value comparison retains the coefficient-field and attached Shimura–Deligne representation construction and finite-extension Chebotarev theorem.
The finite-symbol perfect pairing retains the earlier dim S_2=g identity and its elementary analytic foundations.
Ramified-character bad-prime classification and the local newvector and classical-adelic comparison statements remain outside the supplied finite trace and support proof.

scholarly_sources.scope: Finite weighted traces, partial matrices and fixed-character Fourier support.

figures.mathematical_role: Finite coset trace and common-level coefficient extraction with exact constants; coefficient equality only at indices prime to the other support primes.

scope: The finite weighted traces and arbitrary finite auxiliary-support theorem are proved for a fixed character. Existence and same-character comparison use this local support provider; their deeper prerequisites and the unrestricted support statement remain separately recorded.
